html:
Vengi was the region of the Godavari and Krishna river deltas in coastal Andhra, and the kingdom of the Eastern Chalukyas who ruled it from 624 for over four centuries.

The kingdom was founded when Pulakeshin II of the Chalukyas of Badami conquered the coast from the Vishnukundinas and set his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana over it. The new line soon went its own way. Its rich rice deltas made Vengi a prize, and for centuries the Rashtrakutas and later Chalukyas fought to control it.

In the 11th century Vengi drew close to the Cholas through royal marriages. King Rajaraja Narendra sponsored the poet Nannaya, whose Telugu version of the Mahabharata began Telugu literature. In 1070 his son became Chola emperor as Kulothunga I, and Vengi was merged into the Chola world.
sum: Vengi was the region of the Godavari and Krishna river deltas in coastal Andhra, and the kingdom of the Eastern Chalukyas who ruled it from 624 for over four centuries.
